note: Named places authored on top of the eleven published registers build_places.py reads. Read by emit_places.py, which MERGES them into base/places.qc + base/places.json, and into base/marks.json under --marks. NO GEOMETRY, NO EXTENT AND NO YEAR IS TYPED IN THIS FILE: the anchor, the span and the first year the name may be drawn are all read out of the shipped footprint the entry names, through _bldgsrc.read_bldg() -- the same function the city encoder reads them with, and the same rule heroes_extra.json keeps. What is authored here is a NAME, the footprint it belongs to, and the reason no register carries it.
the_name_is_the_authored_part: Every other row in base/places.* takes its name from a register that published it, and its `src` says which. These rows do not, and their `src` says THAT: it names this file. A reader who opens the provenance sees a path in this repository where the others show a DataSF dataset id, which is the honest signal and is exactly what base/heroes.json already does for Sutro Tower. Nothing here may state a fact the record does not carry -- an entry names a building and points at the pages; it does not narrate them.

names.why: THE RECORD'S OWN WORDS, and deliberately not the fuller name it is usually given. Resolution No. 21068 (New Series) writes `Board of Trustees, Christian Science Church, at southeast corner of Clement street and Funston avenue` and that is the whole of what the City calls it. The building is often named as the Fourth Church of Christ, Scientist, and this file will NOT write that: the same corpus puts the Fourth Church at 5509 Geary Boulevard in 1944 (journalofproceed39part2sanfrich, leaf 255, a $374.19 claim after a police car hit the premises), so the ordinal is contested by the record itself. The unqualified name is what two sources agree on.

AUTHORED, AND NOT READ OFF ANY PUBLISHER THIS PIPELINE TOUCHES. 2009 is the year the Internet Archive acquired 300 Funston Avenue and made it its headquarters. No register in build_places.py's list records a change of occupant -- DataSF publishes what the City owns, designates and rates, not who moved into a private building -- so there is no dataset id to put behind this and the row does not pretend there is: `src` names this file and `yrule` takes the rung that says the year came from us. If that year is wrong it is wrong here, in one line, where a reader can see who wrote it.

places.an: THE FOOTPRINT IS PUBLISHED; THE IDENTIFICATION IS MEASURED. `at` is the shipped ring's own fingerprint -- its vertex mean, its vertex count and its area -- and emit_places.py refuses to write unless the register on disk still carries a ring that matches it. That is heroes_extra.json's index-independence rule, kept for the same reason: a footprint rescue that inserts records ahead of this one shifts `b`, and a seed that trusted the integer alone would silently name the wrong building. The ring is 1,344 m2 on 20 vertices and 15 m tall, which is the 98th percentile of the 166,166 footprints this map draws; every other ring within 40 m of it is a 140-306 m2 house. It is the only structure of that scale on the corner, and it sits 27.7 m from the Internet Archive's own published position for 300 Funston Avenue.
places.why: NO REGISTER THIS PIPELINE READS NAMES IT, and the list is the point of the sentence -- checked one by one, the way Sutro Tower's entry in heroes_extra.json was: DataSF 97yj-54sx Article 10 landmarks and rzic-39gi -- no. ejht-vp5d Article 11 Rating -- no, it covers the downtown conservation districts. gtr9-ntp6 Recreation and Parks Properties, ib5c-xgwu Recreation and Parks Facilities, nc68-ngbr City Facilities, gtnh-hgvs City Lands -- no, and correctly so: 300 Funston is private ground and none of those registers reaches it. 5kya-mfst Tall Building Inventory -- no, at 15 m. 6adp-a5yv Schools_College, 7e7j-59qk Schools, 65ik-7wqd Privately Owned Public Open Spaces -- no. US National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places -- no, there is no Funston Avenue row in it. The nearest named place the map already draws is Sutro Elementary, 147 m away. So the map draws the building and has nothing to write over it, which is the same gap this file's pattern was built to close.
places.record: WHAT THE CITY'S OWN RECORD SAYS ABOUT THIS CORNER, and it is a corroboration rather than a flourish. The assessor's secured roll (DataSF wv5m-vpq2, the `yr` this map already ships on the footprint) dates the structure 1922, with the FLAG_NOYEAR sentinel clear -- so that is a published year and not the 1906 fallback. One year later, on 19 November 1923, the Board of Supervisors passed Resolution No. 21068 (New Series), a list of oil-tank and boiler permits, and one line of it reads `Board of Trustees, Christian Science Church, at southeast corner of Clement street and Funston avenue` -- an oil storage tank of 1,500 gallons capacity, in the same list as the Wigwam Theater on Capp Street and the Roman Catholic Archbishop on Twenty-ninth. Journal of proceedings, 1923 (journalofproceed1923sanfrich), leaf 1295. Two publishers, one year apart, on the same corner.
places.not_claimed: That the 1923 permit and this footprint are the same building is what the two sources JOINTLY support -- a church at that corner in 1923, a 1922 structure of church scale on it now -- and it is not a line either source writes. Nothing in the City's record connects the corner to the Internet Archive; the organisation's occupancy is a fact about the present, not about the minutes, and no copy drawn from this row may imply otherwise.
